title: Power outage
summary: Before, during and after an outage: food, heat and cold, medical devices, generators, and downed lines.

blocks.text: Report outages and downed lines to Dominion Energy at **866-366-4357**. Stay **at least 30 feet** away from a downed line, and treat every line as live.

items: List everything in your home that runs on electricity. Plan backup power (batteries, power bank) for what matters.
A flashlight for every person. Check whether your home phone works without power.
Ask your medical provider for a plan for electric medical devices and for refrigerated medicines, and how long they can stay warm.
Install CO alarms with battery backup on **every level**.
Keep enough non-perishable food and water.
Find out where heating or cooling centers open.
**Keep the fridge and freezer closed.** Fridge: about 4 hours. Full freezer: about 48 hours. Use a thermometer and a cooler with ice.
Go to a community location with power if the heat or cold gets extreme.
**Never heat your home with a gas stove or oven.** Never use a grill, camp stove or generator indoors.
Generators and fuel stay outdoors, **at least 20 feet** from windows, doors and attached garages.
Unplug or switch off appliances and electronics to avoid surge damage when power returns.

blocks.text: Related guides: fridge and freezer rules, generator safety, carbon monoxide, phone battery.

items: Throw out food that was at 40°F or higher for 2 hours or more, or smells, looks or feels wrong. **When in doubt, throw it out.**

If power was out more than a day, discard refrigerated medicines unless the label says otherwise, and ask your doctor or pharmacist for replacements. **Insulin: see the T1D insulin storage guide first.**
Watch for power surges or spikes when power returns.

blocks.text: Henrico Emergency Management: **(804) 501-5162** (Mon-Fri, 8:00-4:30). 211 Virginia: dial **2-1-1** for shelter and resources.
